transcript: So a tight deadline, the one I remember is our first audit after the company raised money. The auditors gave us a list of about eighty items and wanted them in two weeks, and we were only three people in finance, and we still had to do the normal month-end at the same time. I made a tracker in a spreadsheet with every item, who owned it and the status, and we went through it every morning for ten minutes. I took the bank and cash items myself because I knew them best. Some items were really hard, like contracts from two years ago that nobody could find, so we had to email the lawyers and wait. We ended up sending most things on time, but about ten items were four or five days late. The auditors were okay with it because we told them in advance. Month-end was also a few days late that month, which my manager wasn't thrilled about. If I did it again I'd ask for more help from other teams earlier, like legal, instead of waiting until we were stuck.
